text: Which of these is NOT a primitive type in Java?
explanation: String is a class in java.lang, not a primitive.

text: What is the default value of an int instance field?
explanation: Numeric instance fields default to zero.

text: Which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed?
explanation: A final class cannot be extended.

text: What does "abc" == new String("abc") evaluate to?
explanation: == compares references; new String creates a distinct object.

text: Which method must be overridden together with equals() to keep hash-based collections correct?
explanation: Equal objects must return equal hash codes.

text: What is printed? int x = 5; x = x++ + ++x; System.out.println(x);
explanation: x++ yields 5 (x becomes 6), ++x yields 7, so 5 + 7 = 12.

text: Checked exceptions must be...
explanation: The compiler enforces handle-or-declare for checked exceptions.

text: Which statement about a finally block is true?
options: It is skipped when an exception is thrown
It runs before the try block
It runs whether or not an exception occurs, unless the JVM exits
It only runs when an exception occurs
explanation: finally always executes except for System.exit or a JVM crash.

text: String immutability means that...
options: Operations like concat return a new String object
A String cannot be assigned to a variable
Strings are stored on the stack
Strings cannot be used as map keys
explanation: String state never changes; modifying methods return new instances.

text: Which class is preferred for building a string inside a loop in single-threaded code?
explanation: StringBuilder is mutable and unsynchronized, so it is fastest here.

text: Which access modifier makes a member visible within the same package and to subclasses in other packages?
explanation: protected = package access plus subclass access.

text: Can a Java 8+ interface contain method implementations?
options: Yes, through default and static methods
Only if it extends an abstract class
explanation: Java 8 introduced default and static interface methods.

text: Method overloading is resolved at...
explanation: Overload selection is static; overriding is dynamic.

text: Integer a = 127, b = 127; Integer c = 128, d = 128; What are a == b and c == d?
explanation: Integer caches values from -128 to 127, so only 127 is reused.

text: Which collection does not allow duplicate elements?
explanation: Set implementations reject duplicates.

text: Which Map implementation maintains insertion order?
explanation: LinkedHashMap keeps a doubly linked list of entries.

text: Time complexity of get(index) on ArrayList vs LinkedList?
explanation: ArrayList is array-backed; LinkedList must traverse nodes.

text: What happens if you remove elements from an ArrayList inside a for-each loop over the same list?
options: Elements are silently skipped and no error occurs
explanation: The fail-fast iterator detects structural modification; use Iterator.remove or removeIf.

text: Which is true for HashMap?
options: One null key and multiple null values allowed
explanation: HashMap permits a single null key.

text: TreeMap keeps its keys in...
explanation: TreeMap is a red-black tree ordered by key.

text: What does List.of(1, 2, 3).add(4) do?
explanation: List.of returns an unmodifiable list.

text: A functional interface has...
explanation: Single abstract method (SAM) types can be targeted by lambdas.

text: Which of these is a terminal stream operation?
explanation: collect triggers the pipeline; the others are intermediate.

text: What does Stream.of(1,2,3).filter(x -> { System.out.print(x); return true; }); print?
explanation: Streams are lazy; without a terminal operation nothing executes.

text: Optional is primarily intended to...
options: Replace every null field in entities
Represent a possibly absent return value
explanation: Optional signals absence in method return types.

text: What is the result of Arrays.asList(3,1,2).stream().sorted().map(x -> x * 2).findFirst().get()?
explanation: Sorted gives 1,2,3; doubling the first gives 2.

text: Which method reference is equivalent to s -> s.toUpperCase()?
explanation: An unbound instance method reference on the type.

text: What does Dependency Injection primarily achieve?
explanation: Dependencies are supplied from outside rather than created internally.

text: What is the default scope of a Spring bean?
explanation: One shared instance per container by default.

text: Which injection style is recommended for mandatory dependencies?
explanation: Constructor injection enables immutability and easy testing.

text: Which annotation marks a persistence-layer bean and enables exception translation?
explanation: @Repository translates persistence exceptions to DataAccessException.

text: Two beans of the same type exist. How do you choose one at the injection point?
explanation: @Qualifier picks by name; @Primary sets a default.

text: Which annotations does @SpringBootApplication combine?
explanation: It is a convenience meta-annotation.

text: What is the default embedded server for spring-boot-starter-web?
explanation: Tomcat is the default servlet container.

text: Where do you typically configure server.port?
explanation: Boot reads externalized configuration from these files.

text: Which property activates the 'dev' profile?
explanation: spring.profiles.active selects active profiles.

text: Which Actuator endpoint do load balancers commonly use as a health check?
explanation: /actuator/health reports UP or DOWN.

text: What does a Spring Boot 'starter' dependency provide?
options: A curated set of transitive dependencies for a feature
explanation: Starters bundle compatible libraries for a capability.

text: Which source overrides a value set in application.properties packaged inside the jar?
explanation: Environment variables rank above packaged application.properties.

text: Which HTTP method is idempotent and typically used to fully replace a resource?
explanation: PUT replaces the target resource; repeating it has the same effect.

text: Which status code indicates a resource was created successfully?
explanation: 201 Created, usually with a Location header.

text: Which annotation binds a URL segment such as /accounts/{id}?
explanation: @PathVariable maps URI template variables.

text: A client sends a payload that fails validation. Which status is most appropriate?
explanation: 400 Bad Request signals a client-side input problem.

text: @RestController is equivalent to...
explanation: Every handler method's return value is written to the response body.

text: Which status means the client is authenticated but not permitted to access the resource?
explanation: 403 Forbidden; 401 means unauthenticated.

text: Which annotation marks a JPA entity's primary key?
explanation: @Id designates the identifier.

text: In Spring Data, a repository method named findByEmailAndActiveTrue(...) results in...
options: A derived query with two conditions
explanation: Query derivation parses the method name.

text: What is the default fetch type of @ManyToOne?
explanation: To-one associations default to EAGER in JPA.

text: By default, @Transactional rolls back on...
explanation: Checked exceptions commit unless rollbackFor is set.

text: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
explanation: HAVING applies to grouped results.

text: An INNER JOIN returns...
options: Only rows that match in both tables
All rows from the left table
explanation: Only matched pairs are returned.

text: What typically speeds up lookups on a frequently filtered column?
explanation: Indexes avoid full table scans.

text: A primary key constraint implies the column values are...
explanation: Primary keys are unique and non-null.

text: Which annotation marks a JUnit 5 test method?
explanation: org.junit.jupiter.api.Test.

text: Mockito's when(...).thenReturn(...) is used to...
options: Create a spy of a database
explanation: Stubbing defines return values for mock calls.

text: @WebMvcTest loads...
options: Only the web layer (controllers, advice, filters)
explanation: It is a test slice for MVC components.

text: A key characteristic of microservices is...
options: One shared database for all services
Independently deployable services organised around business capabilities
explanation: Autonomy and independent deployment define microservices.

text: What does volatile guarantee?
explanation: volatile provides visibility and ordering, not atomicity.

text: Why is count++ on a shared int unsafe across threads?
explanation: Two threads can read the same value and lose an update.

text: What is the best replacement for a heavily contended shared counter?
explanation: LongAdder scales best under high contention.

text: What does ExecutorService.shutdown() do?
options: Stops accepting new tasks and lets submitted ones finish
Blocks until all tasks are done
explanation: shutdownNow() is the one that interrupts tasks.

text: What is the difference between CompletableFuture.thenApply and thenCompose?
options: thenCompose flattens a function that returns a CompletionStage
explanation: thenCompose is the flatMap of futures.

text: Which map is designed for high-concurrency access without locking the whole map?
explanation: ConcurrentHashMap uses fine-grained locking and CAS.

text: Which set of conditions is required for a deadlock?
options: Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait
explanation: The four Coffman conditions.

text: In Java 8+, when does a HashMap bucket become a balanced tree?
options: When the load factor is exceeded
When a bucket's chain exceeds 8 nodes and capacity is at least 64
explanation: Treeification limits worst-case lookups to O(log n).

text: What happens if a key's hashCode changes after it is inserted into a HashMap?
options: The entry may become unreachable via get
explanation: The entry sits in the bucket for its old hash.

text: Which class is best for a FIFO queue in single-threaded code?
explanation: ArrayDeque is fast and has no synchronization overhead.

text: Comparator.comparing(Emp::getDept).thenComparing(Emp::getSalary, Comparator.reverseOrder()) sorts by...
explanation: The reverse comparator applies only to the salary key.

text: Collectors.groupingBy(Txn::getAccount, Collectors.summingLong(Txn::getAmount)) returns (account is a String)...
explanation: The downstream collector sums per key.

text: What is the difference between map and flatMap on streams?
options: flatMap flattens nested streams into one stream
explanation: flatMap maps each element to a stream and concatenates them.

text: Why can list.parallelStream().forEach(result::add) with an ArrayList result give wrong output?
options: forEach is not allowed on parallel streams
explanation: Use collect() instead of side-effecting a shared list.

text: Records (Java 16+) are best described as...
options: Immutable data carriers with generated equals, hashCode and toString
explanation: Records are transparent carriers of their components.

text: Pattern matching for instanceof allows you to...
options: Write if (obj instanceof String s) and use s directly
explanation: It combines the type test and the cast.

text: Where are objects created with new allocated?
explanation: Escape analysis aside, objects live on the heap.

text: What replaced PermGen in Java 8?
explanation: Class metadata moved to native Metaspace.

text: OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace most likely indicates...
options: Too many objects on the heap
Class metadata growth such as a classloader leak
explanation: Often seen with repeated redeploys or dynamic proxies.

text: What is the default garbage collector on server-class machines in Java 11+?
explanation: G1 became the default in Java 9.

text: Why might @Transactional on a private method have no effect?
options: Proxy-based Spring AOP does not intercept private methods
explanation: Only calls that pass through the proxy are advised.

text: Method A calls @Transactional method B in the same bean. What happens?
options: The transactional advice is bypassed because the call does not go through the proxy
explanation: Self-invocation skips the proxy.

text: A prototype bean is injected into a singleton. What does the singleton hold?
options: The same instance for its lifetime unless ObjectProvider or lookup injection is used
A new instance per method call automatically
explanation: Injection happens once at singleton creation.

text: What is the key difference between @Bean methods in @Configuration vs @Component classes?
options: @Configuration classes are CGLIB-proxied, so inter-bean calls return the container singleton
explanation: In 'lite' mode, calling another @Bean method creates a new instance.

text: How do you bind a group of related properties to a typed object?
explanation: Type-safe binding with validation support.

text: @ConditionalOnMissingBean is used to...
options: Register a bean only if no bean of that type exists
explanation: This is how auto-configuration backs off to user beans.

text: How is exception handling centralized across controllers?
explanation: Advice classes apply to all controllers.

text: What is the best practice for secrets in cloud deployments?
options: Print them to logs for debugging
Use environment variables or a secret manager
explanation: Secrets should never live in source control.

text: A Spring Boot fat jar can run with java -jar because...
options: Spring Boot's launcher loads classes from the nested jars
Maven extracts the jars at build time
The JVM natively supports nested jars
explanation: The Boot loader provides a custom class loader.

text: With spring.jpa.open-in-view=true (the default)...
options: The persistence context stays open through view rendering, which can hide lazy-loading problems
The session closes right after each repository call
explanation: Boot logs a warning because of this.

text: What is the N+1 select problem?
options: One query for the parent list plus one query per parent for an association
explanation: It surfaces when lazy associations are accessed in a loop.

text: How do you fix N+1 queries in Spring Data JPA?
explanation: Fetch the association in the same query.

text: Optimistic locking in JPA is implemented with...
explanation: The version is checked and incremented on update.

text: CascadeType.REMOVE on a @OneToMany association means...
options: The parent is deleted when a child is removed
Children are deleted when the parent is removed
explanation: Removal cascades from parent to children.

text: When does LazyInitializationException occur?
options: When too many eager fetches are configured
When a lazy association is accessed after the persistence context is closed
explanation: The proxy can no longer load its data.

text: What does Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW do?
options: Suspends the current transaction and starts a new one
explanation: Useful for audit logging that must commit independently.

text: What is the best approach for returning large result sets?
options: Page/size or cursor parameters with metadata
explanation: Pagination bounds response size and latency.

text: In payment APIs, an idempotency key header prevents...
explanation: The server returns the original result for a repeated key.

text: HATEOAS means...
options: Responses include links to related resources and actions
explanation: Clients navigate the API through hypermedia.

text: Which status code is used for rate-limited requests?
explanation: 429 Too Many Requests, often with Retry-After.

text: Which API versioning approach is commonly used?
explanation: Both approaches are widely used, each with trade-offs.

text: What is the purpose of an API gateway?
options: A single entry point handling routing, authentication and rate limiting
explanation: It centralizes cross-cutting edge concerns.

text: Service discovery (for example Eureka) solves...
explanation: Clients resolve logical names to live instances.

text: The circuit breaker pattern prevents...
options: Cascading failures by failing fast when a dependency is unhealthy
explanation: It trips open after repeated failures.

text: Which library is commonly used for circuit breaking in Spring Boot 3?
explanation: Hystrix is in maintenance mode; Resilience4j is the standard.

text: Distributed tracing correlates a request across services using...
options: Trace and span IDs propagated in headers
explanation: For example W3C traceparent headers.

text: What is the main trade-off of the database-per-service pattern?
options: Cross-service queries and consistency become harder (eventual consistency)
explanation: Data ownership improves but queries span services.

text: Where does Spring Security apply authentication in a servlet web app?
explanation: SecurityFilterChain runs before controllers.

text: A JWT signature ensures...
explanation: Signed JWTs are readable by anyone; they are not encrypted.

text: How should user passwords be stored?
options: Hashed with an adaptive algorithm such as BCrypt
As plain text in a secure database
explanation: Adaptive, salted hashing resists brute force.

text: How does @DataJpaTest differ from @SpringBootTest?
options: @DataJpaTest loads only the JPA slice, typically with an embedded database
explanation: Slices keep tests fast and focused.

text: Testcontainers is used for...
options: Starting real dependencies (database, Kafka) in Docker for integration tests
explanation: It gives production-like integration tests.

text: What does @MockBean (or @MockitoBean in newer versions) do?
options: Replaces a bean in the Spring context with a Mockito mock
explanation: The mock is injected wherever the bean is used.

text: In Kafka, message ordering is guaranteed...
explanation: Ordering is per partition.

text: What does a Kafka consumer group guarantee?
options: Each partition is consumed by only one consumer in the group
explanation: Partitions are the unit of parallelism.

text: Which of these establishes a happens-before relationship?
options: Releasing and then acquiring the same lock
A volatile write followed by a read of the same variable
Thread.start() before actions in the started thread
explanation: All three are happens-before rules in the JMM.

text: Virtual threads (Java 21) are best suited for...
explanation: They make thread-per-request cheap for I/O-bound services.

text: In Java 21, a virtual thread gets pinned to its carrier notably when...
options: It blocks inside a synchronized block or native call
explanation: Prefer ReentrantLock around blocking calls in Java 21.

text: The ForkJoinPool common pool is used by default for...
options: Parallel streams and CompletableFuture async methods without an executor
explanation: Blocking work there can starve other users of the pool.

text: Why prefer a bounded queue for a ThreadPoolExecutor in production?
options: It provides backpressure and avoids memory exhaustion
explanation: Unbounded queues hide overload until the heap runs out.

text: ReentrantReadWriteLock gives the most benefit when...
explanation: Multiple readers can hold the lock simultaneously.

text: The G1 collector divides the heap into...
explanation: Regions let G1 collect the garbage-richest areas first.

text: A heap dump shows a growing HashMap held by a static field. What is the likely issue?
options: A memory leak from an unbounded static cache
explanation: Static roots keep entries reachable forever.

text: Which JVM flag writes a heap dump automatically on OutOfMemoryError?
explanation: Pair it with -XX:HeapDumpPath.

text: JIT compilation improves performance by...
options: Compiling hot bytecode to native code at runtime
explanation: HotSpot profiles and optimizes hot paths.

text: Escape analysis allows the JVM to...
options: Scalar-replace or stack-allocate objects that do not escape
explanation: It also enables lock elision.

text: ZGC's primary design goal is...
options: Very low pause times largely independent of heap size
explanation: Most work happens concurrently.

text: How does Spring Boot 3 discover auto-configuration classes?
explanation: The imports file replaced spring.factories for auto-configuration.

text: Which Spring stack targets non-blocking, high-concurrency I/O?
options: Spring WebFlux on Netty with Project Reactor
explanation: WebFlux is built on Reactive Streams.

text: How is graceful shutdown enabled in Spring Boot?
explanation: In-flight requests get a grace period to complete.

text: What is a known risk of @Async without a configured executor in older Spring versions?
options: It may create a new thread per task
It uses the Tomcat request thread
explanation: SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor does not pool threads.

text: Hibernate's first-level cache is scoped to...
explanation: It is always on and per persistence context.

text: What is the effect of IDENTITY id generation on Hibernate batch inserts?
options: JDBC insert batching is effectively disabled
explanation: Hibernate must execute each insert to learn the id; use SEQUENCE for batching.

text: Which is a read-only query optimization in Spring?
explanation: Hibernate can skip dirty checking.

text: A pessimistic write lock in JPA typically translates to...
explanation: The row is locked until the transaction ends.

text: The Saga pattern addresses...
options: Distributed transactions via a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions
explanation: It replaces two-phase commit across services.

text: In a choreography-based saga...
options: Services react to each other's events without a central coordinator
A central coordinator directs each step
explanation: Orchestration uses a central coordinator instead.

text: The transactional outbox pattern solves...
options: The dual-write problem between a database update and a message publish
explanation: The event is stored in the same transaction and relayed later.

text: The bulkhead pattern isolates...
options: Resources such as thread pools or connections per dependency to contain failures
explanation: One slow dependency cannot exhaust all resources.

text: The strangler fig pattern is used for...
options: Incrementally migrating a monolith by routing features to new services
explanation: The legacy system is replaced piece by piece.

text: Retries with exponential backoff and jitter help avoid...
explanation: Jitter de-synchronizes clients.

text: Why are idempotent consumers needed with most message brokers?
options: Brokers typically deliver at least once, so duplicates occur
explanation: Redelivery after failures produces duplicates.

text: Spring Cloud Config provides...
explanation: Configuration is served from a repository.

text: Consumer-driven contract testing (Pact, Spring Cloud Contract) verifies that...
options: The provider's API meets its consumers' expectations
explanation: Breaking changes are caught before deployment.

text: ETag with If-None-Match enables...
options: Conditional GETs that return 304 when the resource is unchanged
explanation: It saves bandwidth and supports caching.

text: What is the REST best practice for a long-running operation such as processing a bulk payment file?
options: Hold the connection until processing is done
Return 202 Accepted with a status resource to poll or a callback
Return 200 immediately with a fake result
explanation: The client tracks progress asynchronously.

text: Which is true for PATCH?
options: It applies partial modifications and is not necessarily idempotent
It is the same as PUT
explanation: Idempotency depends on the patch semantics.

text: OpenAPI (Swagger) is used for...
options: Describing and documenting the REST API contract
explanation: It enables docs, client generation and contract testing.

text: What triggers a Kafka consumer group rebalance?
options: A consumer joining or leaving, or exceeding the session timeout or max poll interval
explanation: Long processing between polls is a common cause.

text: The Kafka idempotent producer (enable.idempotence=true) prevents...
options: Duplicates caused by producer retries within a partition
explanation: Sequence numbers let the broker drop retried duplicates.

text: How do you guarantee ordering of all events for a given account in Kafka?
options: Use one consumer group per message
Use the account ID as the message key
explanation: Same key means same partition, which means ordered.

text: A dead-letter topic or queue is used for...
explanation: It keeps the main flow moving and preserves failures for analysis.

text: What does acks=all mean for a Kafka producer?
options: The leader waits for all in-sync replicas to acknowledge
explanation: Combine with min.insync.replicas for durability.

text: Which OAuth2 flow is recommended for SPAs and mobile apps?
explanation: PKCE protects the code exchange for public clients.

text: Service-to-service authentication without a user typically uses...
options: Client credentials grant or mutual TLS
explanation: Machine identities authenticate themselves.

text: CSRF protection is most relevant when...
options: Only bearer tokens in headers are used
Authentication relies on cookies sent automatically by the browser
explanation: CSRF exploits ambient browser credentials.

text: How should a resource server validate JWT access tokens?
options: Verify signatures with the issuer's JWKS public keys and check claims
Query the user database on every request only
explanation: Also validate exp, iss and aud.

text: Which pattern does Spring's JdbcTemplate primarily exemplify?
explanation: It fixes the workflow and delegates the variable steps via callbacks.

text: The Strategy pattern is best for...
explanation: For example, choosing a fee calculation per payment type.

text: Why is double-checked locking for a singleton broken without volatile?
options: Instruction reordering can publish a partially constructed object
synchronized does not work in singletons
explanation: volatile prevents the unsafe publication.

text: The Decorator pattern adds behaviour...
options: Dynamically, by wrapping objects that share the same interface
explanation: java.io streams are a classic example.

text: During a network partition, the CAP theorem says a distributed system must choose between...
explanation: Partition tolerance is not optional in practice.

text: The cache-aside pattern means...
options: The cache writes to the database automatically
The application loads data into the cache on a miss and invalidates it after writing to the database
The database pushes updates to the cache
explanation: Also known as lazy loading.

text: For account balance reads that require strict consistency, which approach is risky?
options: Serving balances from asynchronously replicated read replicas without accounting for lag
explanation: Replica lag can show stale balances.

text: Horizontal scaling means...
options: Adding more CPU to one server
explanation: Vertical scaling adds resources to a single node.

text: Consistent hashing helps by...
options: Minimizing key remapping when nodes join or leave
explanation: Only about 1/n of the keys move.

text: Per the SQL standard, which isolation level prevents non-repeatable reads but may allow phantom reads?
explanation: Phantoms are only prevented by SERIALIZABLE in the standard.

text: A composite index on (account_id, created_at) best serves...
explanation: Leftmost-prefix rule plus index-ordered scan.

text: EXPLAIN (an execution plan) is used to...
options: Analyze how the database executes a query
explanation: It reveals scans, joins and index use.

text: Why does keyset (seek) pagination outperform OFFSET on large tables?
options: It avoids scanning and discarding the skipped rows
It is the only standard SQL option
explanation: WHERE id > last_seen uses the index directly.

text: In a payment system, what is the practical way to achieve an exactly-once effect?
options: At-least-once delivery with idempotent processing and deduplication keys
Two-phase commit across all services and third parties
Relying on the network for exactly-once delivery
explanation: Effect-once is achieved at the application level.

text: A globally distributed ledger needs strong consistency. Which approach fits?
explanation: Consensus provides linearizable writes across sites.

text: Event sourcing stores...
options: State changes as an immutable sequence of events from which state is derived
explanation: Current state is a fold over the events.

text: CQRS is most justified when...
options: Read and write workloads or models differ significantly in shape or scale
The team is small and the domain is simple
explanation: Otherwise the added complexity is rarely worth it.

text: What is the primary cost of combining CQRS with event sourcing?
options: More complexity, eventually consistent read models and event schema evolution
explanation: These costs must be weighed against the benefits.

text: To achieve an RPO near zero across regions for core banking data you need...
options: Synchronous replication or quorum writes across sites, accepting the added latency
explanation: Asynchronous replication can lose in-flight writes.

text: RTO measures...
options: The maximum acceptable time to restore service after an outage
The maximum acceptable data loss window
explanation: RPO measures data loss; RTO measures downtime.

text: Backpressure in streaming systems means...
options: Consumers signal producers to slow down to avoid overload
explanation: Reactive Streams formalizes it with request(n).

text: A hot partition in a sharded datastore is best mitigated by...
options: Better key design, such as salting or composite keys, to spread load
explanation: Skewed keys concentrate traffic on one shard.

text: A 99.9% monthly availability SLO allows roughly how much downtime in a 30-day month?
explanation: 43,200 minutes x 0.1% = 43.2 minutes.

text: Noisy-neighbour problems in multi-tenant SaaS are mitigated by...
options: Per-tenant quotas, rate limits and resource isolation
explanation: Fairness must be enforced per tenant.

text: Which is a sign that a synchronous call chain should become asynchronous?
options: Long fan-out chains where latency and failure probability compound across hops
explanation: Availability multiplies across synchronous hops.

text: In Domain-Driven Design, a bounded context defines...
options: A boundary within which a domain model and its ubiquitous language are consistent
explanation: Each context owns its model.

text: An anti-corruption layer is used to...
options: Translate between your domain model and a legacy or external model
explanation: It keeps external concepts from leaking into your domain.

text: Service mesh sidecars (Istio, Linkerd) typically provide...
options: mTLS, retries, traffic shifting and telemetry outside application code
explanation: Networking concerns move into the platform.

text: In a canary deployment...
options: A small share of traffic goes to the new version and is increased gradually
explanation: Blue-green switches all traffic at once.

text: What is the safest way to change a schema shared across service versions without downtime?
explanation: Old and new versions keep working during the transition.

text: A 'distributed monolith' is characterized by...
options: Services that must be deployed together because of tight coupling
explanation: It combines the costs of both styles.

text: Conway's law implies that...
options: System architecture mirrors the organization's communication structure
explanation: Team topology shapes system boundaries.

text: Platform teams and 'golden paths' aim to...
options: Reduce cognitive load through paved, self-service tooling
explanation: Teams move faster on supported defaults.

text: What is a reasonable timeout strategy for inter-service calls with strict latency budgets?
options: Use the same large timeout everywhere
Propagate deadlines along the call chain, with per-hop timeouts smaller than the caller's
explanation: Callers should not wait longer than their own budget.

text: When would you choose gRPC over REST for internal service calls?
options: For public browser APIs without a proxy
For low latency, strongly typed contracts and streaming between services
explanation: Protobuf over HTTP/2 is compact and typed.

text: Kafka exactly-once semantics in stream processing rely on...
options: Idempotent producers, transactions and read_committed consumers
explanation: Offsets and outputs are committed atomically.

text: Kafka log compaction retains...
options: At least the latest value for each key
explanation: Useful for changelog and state topics.

text: Schema evolution in event-driven systems is best governed by...
options: A schema registry with compatibility rules (backward/forward)
explanation: Compatibility checks run before a schema is registered.

text: What happens if you increase the partitions of an existing keyed Kafka topic?
options: Per-key ordering can break because keys map to different partitions
explanation: The hash-mod mapping changes.

text: Kafka fits better than a traditional queue (RabbitMQ, MQ) when you need...
options: Replayable, high-throughput event streams with multiple independent consumers
explanation: The log model supports replay and fan-out.

text: What is best practice for handling a poison-pill message?
options: Bounded retries, then route it to a DLQ with alerting
explanation: Otherwise the partition is blocked.

text: The core principle of zero-trust architecture is...
options: Never trust, always verify: authenticate and authorize every request regardless of network location
explanation: Network location grants no implicit trust.

text: For PCI-DSS scoped card data, a common architectural strategy is...
options: Tokenization to minimize the systems that store the PAN
explanation: Fewer systems in scope means less risk and audit effort.

text: Secrets rotation at scale is best handled by...
options: A vault or secret manager issuing dynamic, short-lived credentials
explanation: Short-lived credentials limit the blast radius.

text: Which defends against replay attacks on signed API requests?
options: Timestamps and nonces with short validity windows
explanation: A captured request cannot be reused later.

text: The principle of least privilege applied to microservices means...
options: Each service gets only the permissions and database grants it needs
explanation: It limits lateral movement after a compromise.

text: A JVM service shows p99 latency spikes every few minutes that correlate with long full GCs. What is the first step?
options: Analyze GC logs and allocation rate, then tune the heap/GC or fix allocation hotspots
explanation: Diagnose before scaling out.

text: Java Flight Recorder (JFR) is used for...
options: Low-overhead profiling and event recording in production
explanation: Analyze recordings in JDK Mission Control.

text: In containers, -XX:MaxRAMPercentage controls...
options: Maximum heap as a percentage of the container memory limit
explanation: The JVM is container-aware since Java 10.

text: AppCDS and GraalVM native image primarily improve...
explanation: Valuable for scale-to-zero and serverless.

text: Little's Law (L = lambda x W) helps you to...
options: Size concurrency, such as thread or connection pools, from throughput and latency
explanation: For example, 200 rps x 0.05 s = 10 concurrent requests.

text: Structured concurrency (preview in Java 21) aims to...
options: Treat related concurrent tasks as a unit with coordinated cancellation and error handling
explanation: Child tasks cannot outlive their scope.

text: Lock-free algorithms typically rely on...
explanation: Retry loops around CAS avoid blocking.

text: False sharing degrades performance when...
options: Threads write independent variables that share a CPU cache line
explanation: Padding (for example @Contended) mitigates it.

text: A distributed lock built on Redis or ZooKeeper must handle...
options: Lease expiry and fencing tokens so stale lock holders cannot corrupt data
explanation: Pauses can outlive the lease.

text: How do you prevent double-spend on concurrent debits of the same account?
options: Check the balance and update it in separate transactions
Cache balances in memory per pod
Serialize per account (row lock, version check or per-key partitioning) and validate the balance in the same transaction
explanation: Check-then-act across transactions is a race.

text: What is the main challenge of sharding a transactions table by customer_id?
options: Cross-shard queries and transactions, such as reporting or transfers between customers on different shards
explanation: Shard keys should match the dominant access pattern.

text: Change Data Capture (for example Debezium) is used to...
options: Stream database changes from the transaction log as events to other systems
explanation: It avoids dual writes from the application.

text: Which is appropriate for an audit trail that must be tamper-evident?
options: Append-only storage with hash chaining or WORM retention
explanation: Any modification breaks the chain.

text: Polyglot persistence is justified when...
options: Different data access patterns genuinely benefit from different stores
The team wants to try new technology
explanation: Every store adds operational cost.

text: How can read-your-writes consistency be achieved in a replicated system?
options: Route a user's reads to the primary or track replication position with session tokens
explanation: The user must never see data older than their own write.

text: Hexagonal (ports and adapters) architecture primarily aims to...
options: Isolate domain logic from infrastructure through ports with pluggable adapters
explanation: The domain has no framework dependencies.

text: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) are used to...
options: Document significant decisions with their context and consequences
explanation: Future readers learn why, not just what.

text: In a build-vs-buy decision for a fraud-detection component, the most important factors are...
options: Total cost of ownership and strategic differentiation versus time-to-market and risk
explanation: Build what differentiates; buy commodity.

text: How should technical debt be managed?
options: Make it visible, quantify its impact and prioritize paydown alongside features
explanation: Debt is a business decision, not only an engineering one.

text: Which API change is backward compatible?
explanation: Tolerant readers ignore unknown fields.

text: Which rate-limiting algorithm allows bursts while enforcing an average rate?
explanation: Tokens accumulate up to the bucket capacity.

text: For partner-facing banking APIs, request integrity and non-repudiation typically use...
options: Mutual TLS plus message signing (for example JWS) with timestamps
An API key in the query string
explanation: The signature binds the payload to the sender.
